title: Are Large Reasoning Models Good Everyday Reasoners? A Comparison with Non-Reasoning Models on Logical Reasoning Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.22538v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) that leverage test-time computation achieve strong performance on mathematical and scientific benchmarks and are increasingly deployed in real-world applications. However, their ability to perform \textit{everyday logical reasoning}, which often departs from textbook formal logic, remains underexplored. In this work, we systematically evaluate how well reasoning models align with everyday reasoning patterns by introducing a benchmark based on linguistic and pragmatic reasoning phenomena. We also compare reasoning models with non-reasoning models under controlled prompting conditions. translated_title: 大型推理模型是优秀的日常推理者吗？与非推理模型在逻辑推理任务上的对比
translated_abstract: 利用测试时计算的大型推理模型（LRMs）在数学和科学基准测试中取得了出色的表现，并越来越多地被部署于实际应用中。然而，它们进行日常逻辑推理的能力——这类推理往往偏离教科书式的形式逻辑——仍然未被充分探索。在本工作中，我们通过引入一个基于语言学和语用推理现象的基准，系统地评估了推理模型与日常推理模式的契合程度。我们还在受控的提示条件下对推理模型与非推理模型进行了比较。我们发现，在许多情况下：(1) 当日常推理偏离形式逻辑规则时，推理模型在日常推理中的表现会出现下降；(2) 一些经过思维链提示的非推理模型在日常推理中的表现优于同类的推理模型；(3) 通过提供额外指令的提示……
tldr: 该研究构建了一个基于语言学与语用推理现象的日常逻辑推理基准，发现大型推理模型在偏离形式逻辑规则的日常推理中表现退化，而某些采用思维链提示的非推理模型在日常推理上甚至优于推理模型。
en_tdlr: This work introduces a benchmark based on linguistic and pragmatic reasoning phenomena and finds that large reasoning models degrade on everyday logical reasoning that deviates from formal logic, with some chain-of-thought prompted non-reasoning models even outperforming reasoning models.
